metadata.description: HPL (LINPACK) double-precision benchmark on the UJEP-LAB cluster, 2026-10-22. Source: UJEP-LAB/benchmarks/hpl (hpl.csv, logs); playbooks opennebula/playbooks/hpl_setup.yml, hpl_run.yml; regenerate with tools/make_hpl_data.py.
metadata.hardware_per_node: 2 x Intel Xeon E5-2650 v4 (12 cores each, 24 cores, 48 threads), 64 GiB DDR4 (62.26 GiB visible), ConnectX-5 EDR 100 Gbit/s
metadata.nodes: 8 computes (Rocky-Compute-1..8) plus 2 heads (Rocky-Head-1/2, Lustre MGS/MDT servers)

software.mpi: Open MPI 4.1.1 (distro), pml ucx over UCX 1.19.1 (rc_verbs/ud_verbs on mlx5_0, RDMA)

metadata.configuration: one MPI rank per socket (2 per node), 12 BLAS threads per rank bound to the socket; NB=192; PFACT right, RFACT Crout, 1ring-modified broadcast, lookahead 1, mix swap; xhpl run from local disk on every node
metadata.matrix_size_rule: N = sqrt(frac * node_memory * nodes / 8) rounded down to a multiple of NB; frac 0.75 for 1 and 5 nodes, 0.70 for 10 nodes
metadata.rpeak_note: Rpeak = nodes x 24 cores x 16 DP FLOP/cycle x 2.2 GHz (nominal base). Observed clocks during the runs averaged about 2.5-2.6 GHz over all logical CPUs (including idle hyper-threads), so efficiency against the nominal figure is not a hard ceiling.
caveats: The 10-node run includes the two Lustre servers (heads), used nice 10 and 70% memory for safety; Lustre stayed responsive (lfs df about 0.014 s).
Single runs, no repetitions; one block size (NB 192); distro OpenBLAS, not Intel MKL.
Power draw was not measured; the lab breaker limit was the reason for the 1 -> 5 -> 10 node ramp.

findings.title: HPL scales almost linearly over InfiniBand
findings.result: 713.5 GFLOPS on 1 node, 3,476.5 on 5 (97.5% scaling), 6,751.0 on all 10 nodes (94.6% scaling, 79.9% of the nominal 8.45 TFLOPS peak); all residual checks PASSED. The fabric and MPI over RDMA cost about 5% at 10 nodes.

findings.title: Distro OpenBLAS: libopenblas.so is the serial build
findings.result: On Rocky 9 libopenblas.so is single-threaded; the threaded build is libopenblasp.so. Linking the former would have made each MPI rank use 1 core instead of 12 without any error.

findings.title: firewalld blocks Open MPI by default
findings.result: ibs1 sits in the public zone with a port whitelist; Open MPI uses dynamic ports, so multi-node launches failed ('unable to complete a TCP connection'). Fixed with a rich rule accepting only the IB subnet 10.0.0.0/24. A 1-node run never notices because it stays on the node.

findings.title: UID mismatch on Compute-3
findings.result: The `user` account has UID 1001 on Compute-3 and 1000 on all other nodes (heads included). Lustre identifies users by UID and the MDS does not know 1001, so `user` on Compute-3 gets 'Permission denied' below /mnt/lustre (root works). Worked around by staging xhpl and the run directory on local disk as root; the mismatch itself is not fixed and also matters for OpenNebula.
